alternatives.root_cause: A feature flag was flipped enabling a slow/failing cart code path, leaving no change records anywhere.
alternatives.why_not: The ~300ms penalty appears on plain GetCart traces that contain no flagd evaluation span at all (tr_a0d56559008c), and flagd's own resolveBoolean spans return in under a millisecond, so the delay is not gated by the flag evaluation path.

alternatives.root_cause: Checkout itself is the broken service because it is where the errors are recorded.
alternatives.why_not: Checkout's spans fail at a flat ~5s ceiling after waiting on cart, and all of its other dependencies answer in milliseconds (tr_dcac8e8dc71f); it is the service that noticed, and its change log is empty (tr_e53387b7d6e3).

alternatives.root_cause: Cart exhausted a connection pool or thread pool, serialising requests behind a scarce resource.
alternatives.why_not: Exhaustion produces queueing that grows with load and usually surfaces rejection or pool-wait errors; instead every operation costs an identical ~300ms with a zero error ratio (tr_6e6b0579589a, tr_a0d56559008c), and short single-op traces show the same 300ms with no concurrency to queue behind.

verdict.summary: Cart's Valkey cart-store operations each began taking a uniform ~300ms (HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE), so cart-dependent calls stacked up and checkout's PlaceOrder blew its ~5s deadline and errored.
verdict.reasoning: Checkout alerted with PlaceOrder spans failing at a flat ~5s deadline (tr_dcac8e8dc71f), which is a caller timing out, not a caller breaking. Walking the traces down, every trace's degrading hop lands inside cart's own store operations, each pinned at almost exactly 300ms regardless of operation type or payload (tr_a0d56559008c); all other downstream services (currency, payment, shipping, product-catalog, email, flagd) return in single-digit milliseconds in the same traces, so the delay is specific to cart's store path and not ambient. Cart itself reports a zero error ratio in both incident and baseline windows (tr_6e6b0579589a) and logs ordinary store calls with no error or exhaustion text (tr_91e6d4a14335) - it is waiting, not failing, which is exactly the dependency_latency shape and rules out freeze (it writes), partition (it reaches its store and flagd), disk_fill and corruption (reads and writes complete successfully, just slowly). Change logs for cart, checkout and flagd are all empty over a 24h window (tr_3d1094179ddd, tr_e257fd0a4e64, tr_e53387b7d6e3), so no artifact or config edit is implicated. Checkout's own log window was empty (tr_356f704dcdfb), consistent with it only timing out rather than producing errors of its own. The alert ordering (cart, then checkout, then frontend, frontend-proxy, load-generator) is the latency propagating outward toward the caller.
open_questions: Whether the latency originates in the Valkey/cart-store backend itself or in an artificial delay injected into cart's store client, since the store is not separately observable as a service here.

Why the ~300ms is so uniform across all operations - this regularity is more typical of an injected sleep than of organic datastore load, but no change record or flag-store observation confirmed either.

Whether a flag flip (flagd change log empty by definition for feature_flag) enabled a slow cart path; the GetCart traces show the 300ms with no flag evaluation span in the path, which argues against it but does not fully exclude it.
Whether restarting cart or its store actually clears the delay, since no remediation was observed.
